historical_reviews.deepseek: Hashing the source and written file checks one direction's integrity only; no timed write including durable sync, read-back copy, per-port identity or negotiated-link proof is captured.
historical_reviews.gpt_v2: Correctly requires per-port negotiated speed and protects media, while leaving authoritative port population and performance thresholds to engineering.
historical_reviews.related_cases: This is physical USB storage-port coverage. It is not satisfied by controller enumeration alone, and USB protocol signaling speed must not be equated to storage payload throughput.
historical_reviews.v3_1: Preserve operator insertion and every-port iteration; bind device serial and mount to each physical port; test both directions with hashes and durable timing; report negotiated USB topology separately from payload rate; quarantine the USB2/USB3 criterion conflict.

original_test_intent: Verify safe bidirectional file transfer, data integrity and acceptable measured throughput on every intended external USB 3.0 port using dedicated test media.
original_method: Map every physical USB 3.0 port to controller/root-hub path; approve a dedicated empty test drive and unique partition/filesystem/mount; record serial/capacity/free space and negotiated USB generation for each insertion; create one approved incompressible file and source hash; time host-to-USB copy plus durable sync, hash the media file, time USB-to-host read-back to a new file and hash it; collect kernel USB/storage errors; safely sync/unmount before moving the same drive to the next port; never overwrite unapproved paths or infer throughput from signaling rate.
manual_activity: An operator supplies dedicated disposable media, identifies/inserts it into each physical port and safely removes it; the agent may run approved guarded bidirectional copies and collect timing/hash/topology evidence.
required_inputs: Authoritative USB 3.0 versus USB 2.0 port population and correction/interpretation of Criteria 3
Physical port labels and controller/root-hub/connector mapping
Dedicated drive model/serial/capacity/partition/filesystem and approved mount/test directory
Approved file size/content, free-space margin, write/read timing method, cache policy and timeout
Expected negotiated USB generation/link speed and separate minimum sustained write/read payload thresholds per port/media
Safe sync/unmount/removal procedure and kernel error/thermal/media abort criteria
safety_requirements: Use only uniquely identified dedicated test media and a newly created approved test directory; refuse an ambiguous device or mount
Verify capacity/free space and resolved device/mount path before every write; never overwrite operator data or a raw device
Keep the media inserted through durable sync and hash completion; safely unmount before removal or port change
Use secure credentials and verified host identity
Do not clear global caches or alter kernel/storage settings unless separately approved; disclose cache effects in results
Stop on disconnect, reset, I/O error, hash mismatch, filesystem warning, abnormal temperature or unexpected kernel event; no automatic retry
agent_execution_scope: Validate device serial, partition, filesystem, mount, free space and physical-port/topology mapping after operator insertion
Create the approved source file and perform guarded timed write, sync, media hash, timed read-back and destination hash
Collect negotiated topology, payload rates and kernel logs per port, then safely unmount on approval
Do not select media/ports, resolve the Master conflict, overwrite existing data, drop caches, retry failures or decide PASS/FAIL
engineer_actions: Resolve USB2/USB3 scope conflict and enumerate required ports
Approve test media/path/file/timing/cache and performance thresholds
Approve safe unmount/removal and abort policy
Review per-port integrity/speed/log evidence and issue the DUT verdict

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: Incomplete and unsafe as written: it assumes `/mnt/usb`, overwrites `x`, measures no throughput and performs no USB-to-host copy; password/host-key options are insecure.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: For each verified port/media mount, use unique guarded paths and approved timing tools for host-to-USB copy plus durable sync and USB-to-host read-back; hash source, media and read-back files, record negotiated topology and preserve full exits/logs.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: Operator USB key insertion, copy to/from media, speed check, all-port repetition, successful-copy intent, Common branch and 15/30-minute estimate are preserved; the conflicting USB2 wording remains pending.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Run identity-bound bidirectional integrity and durable-throughput checkpoints on every approved physical USB 3.0 port, recording topology and payload rates separately.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds destructive-path guards, serial/port identity, both copy directions, three-way hashes, durable timing, cache disclosure, negotiated topology and per-port thresholds.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: A single host-to-media copy/hash cannot prove read-back direction, all ports or speed; negotiated 5/10/20 Gb/s signaling does not equal storage throughput.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Drive/controller/filesystem cache and media quality dominate measured throughput; fixed limits must be project/media-specific.

project_override_considerations: Until engineering resolves Criteria 3, do not silently convert USB2 ports into USB3 expectations or omit any ports. Preserve the Master wording and report the conflict.
expected_evidence: Resolved required-port matrix and physical label/controller/root-hub mapping
Per-port negotiated USB topology/generation and insertion timestamps
Source file identity/size/hash, timed host-to-USB plus sync output and media-file hash
Timed USB-to-host read-back output and read-back hash matched to source
Per-port write/read payload rates versus approved thresholds, kernel USB/storage logs, safe unmount and engineer verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Item and Procedure explicitly target every USB 3.0 port, but Criteria 3 explicitly says every USB 2.0 port should match USB 3.0 speed. USB2 signaling cannot normally meet USB3 signaling speed, so the authoritative port scope/expectation cannot be inferred safely.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The conflict prevents a final DUT verdict but not the static review or guarded evidence collection for identified USB3 ports; it remains RPUC with an engineering decision pending rather than globally BLOCKED.

engineering_decision_pending.question: Resolve Reliability row153 Wistron-HW Robust-00030-V002: correct or interpret Criteria 3 (`All USB 2.0 port should match USB 3.0 speed`) against the USB3 item/procedure and provide the authoritative physical-port matrix; approve dedicated drive/serial/filesystem/mount/test path, bidirectional file size/content, timing/cache/sync method, negotiated generation oracle, separate sustained write/read thresholds per port/media, safe unmount/removal and I/O/hash/kernel-log abort criteria.

review_improvement: Exposes the Master USB2/USB3 contradiction and upgrades a one-way untimed overwrite into guarded per-port bidirectional integrity, durable throughput and topology evidence without resolving the conflict by guesswork.
independent_technical_reasoning: The source explicitly says copy to/from, so both directions are coverage requirements. The proposed copy only writes to media and a hash verifies content at rest but not a separately read-back file or read speed. `sync` affects durability and timing, while page and device caches can inflate measurements. Also USB protocol rate is not a storage throughput guarantee. Most importantly, requiring USB2 ports to match USB3 speed contradicts the named USB3 scope and physical bandwidth tiers; engineering must choose the intended population and thresholds before verdict.
